metadata.case_name: WU HO YAN v. CHAN LAI YUNG YVONNE

injuries.description: small amount of marrow edema at the right sacroiliac joint which was compatible with osteitis condensa ilii, though early inflammatory sacroiliitis was difficult to be completely excluded.
source: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) was performed on both hips of the plaintiff. It showed that there was small amount of marrow edema at the right sacroiliac joint which was compatible with osteitis condensa ilii, though early inflammatory sacroiliitis was difficult to be completely excluded.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: right foot chronic regional pain syndrome / right foot dorsum neuropathic pain
source: The provisional diagnosis was right foot chronic regional pain syndrome.

physical examination suggested that the plaintiff had sacroiliac joint pain and allodynia over right foot dorsum. Besides, right foot dorsum neuropathic pain and right sacroiliac joint pain was diagnosed.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of cutaneous sensory nerve at ankle or foot level

injuries.description: superficial abrasions over elbows, right buttock, chin and both legs
injuries.body_part: elbows; right buttock; chin; both legs
source: superficial abrasions over elbows, right buttock, chin and both legs;

manifestations.description: The plaintiff said that she still feels hip pain after standing for 10 to 15 minutes. She described the pain as like being jabbed by 20 needles.
complaints of persistent right foot pain
swelling and tenderness over the right medial foot
She could walk unaided for 20 to 30 minutes.

treatments_received.treatment: admission to Pok Oi Hospital for treatment and discharge same day
source: After the accident, the plaintiff was admitted to Pok Oi Hospital for treatment. ... She was discharged on the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: physiotherapy (Prince of Wales Hospital) for 4 months between June and November 2009
source: Besides, the plaintiff received physiotherapy treatment from the Prince of Wales Hospital for 4 months between June and November 2009. The treatment was stopped as the progress became static.

treatments_received.treatment: referral to Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology of the Prince of Wales Hospital and MRI of both hips (November 2009)
source: In June 2009, because of the plaintiff’s complaints of persistent right foot pain, she was referred by a private medical practitioner to the Department of Orthopaedics & Traumatology of the Prince of Wales Hospital.
In November 2009, Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) was performed on both hips of the plaintiff.

treatments_received.treatment: pain management at Department of Anaesthesiology & Operating Services of Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital; discharged from pain clinic to out-patient department
source: In June 2009, the plaintiff was referred to the Department of Anaesthesiology & Operating Services of Alice Ho Miu Ling Nethersole Hospital for pain management.
In view of her stable pain condition, she was later discharged from the pain clinic to out-patient department for further management.

treatments_future.treatment: MRI arranged on 2013-07-26 to rule out spinal pathology
source: Another MRI is arranged on 26 July 2013 to rule out spinal pathology.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: She complains that she has difficulties coping with household chores.
